clinicalStatus: Draft inventory and reference. All 668 entries await independent nephrologist and renal-pharmacist review. Not approved for bedside prescribing.

referenceScope.bnfStatus: Monographs inaccessible; comparison pending. Edition existence checked with publisher only.

acetaminophen.title: Acetaminophen / paracetamol
acetaminophen.text: Generally kidney-safe at recommended doses. Check combination cold/pain products to prevent duplicate dosing. Liver disease requires separate advice. No numeric CKD or dialysis regimen is curated here.

systemic-nsaid.title: Systemic NSAID safety
systemic-nsaid.text: Systemic NSAIDs can cause AKI and worsen CKD. NKF advises avoidance in CKD, especially eGFR <60; do not self-treat. If a clinician selects one, use an individual risk assessment, the lowest dose and shortest duration. This is a class warning, not a dialysis dosing protocol.

topical-pain.title: Topical pain products
topical-pain.text: Label-directed topical pain products generally have lower kidney risk. Diclofenac gel has less systemic exposure than oral diclofenac. Do not exceed application limits. Lower systemic exposure does not establish safety for every product or patient.

aspirin.title: Distinguish aspirin indications
aspirin.text: Analgesic/high-dose aspirin carries NSAID kidney risks. Do not use this warning to stop prescribed low-dose antiplatelet aspirin; verify the indication and exact product with the treating team.

antacid.title: Antacid ingredients in CKD
antacid.text: Calcium, magnesium, bismuth and aluminium ingredients can accumulate in CKD. Check the exact combination and renal-team advice. NKF advises avoiding aluminium-containing products because of brain toxicity. This does not define prescribed phosphate-binder dosing.

h2.title: H2 blocker accumulation
h2.text: H2 blockers such as cimetidine and nizatidine are renally cleared and may require lower doses or longer intervals. This safety note does not provide a renal regimen; obtain a product-specific recommendation.

ppi.title: OTC proton pump inhibitors
ppi.text: Discuss OTC PPI use with the kidney team. Reassess prolonged treatment and potential kidney/mineral adverse effects. An absence of renal dose reduction does not justify unsupervised long-term use.

phosphate.title: Sodium phosphate bowel preparations
phosphate.text: Oral sodium phosphate bowel preparations can cause kidney injury and should be avoided in CKD. Do not extrapolate an alternative bowel-preparation prescription from this warning.

decongestant.title: Cold remedies and decongestants
decongestant.text: Kidney Care UK advises avoiding decongestant-containing cold remedies, including pseudoephedrine and phenylephrine, especially with hypertension. Check all active ingredients in combination products.

constipation.title: Constipation products
constipation.text: Kidney Care UK lists senna as an option. Bulk-forming ispaghula/psyllium may be unsuitable with fluid restriction. Persistent constipation and PD-related constipation need renal-team advice; no dose is selected here.

diarrhoea.title: Diarrhoea and rehydration
diarrhoea.text: Kidney Care UK lists loperamide as an option for selected minor diarrhoea. Severe illness needs assessment. Use oral rehydration salts only if the treating team recommends them; fluid and electrolyte restrictions matter.

drugs.name: Acyclovir
drugs.formulation: IV renal tables only · oral dose curation pending
drugs.kidneyMetric: CrCl · mL/min; adult Cockcroft–Gault in Nebraska protocol
drugs.summary: Selected IV HSV/VZV renal regimens; oral acyclovir is not covered by these dose rows.

ckd.notes: Source uses adjusted body weight in obesity. Verify fractional CrCl gaps and the exact indication; monitor renal function and neurotoxicity.

ihd.notes: Give daily, after HD on HD days; not only after dialysis sessions.

crrt.notes: CVVHD only, not CVVH/CVVHDF or a universal CRRT regimen. Reassess residual function, treatment interruptions and actual delivered flow. Evidence above 2 L/h is limited.
crrt.settingMeasure: Nebraska CVVHD · dialysate flow 1, 2 or 3–4 L/h

sled.notes: The reviewed PIRRT source explicitly reports no data. No dose is inferred from CKD, IHD or CRRT.

drugs.considerations: Use an appropriate infusion rate and hydration plan; the obese dosing-weight recommendation is source specific. No oral or intraperitoneal dose is inferred.
drugs.completeness: Selected adult source-specific indications only. Regimens do not cover every infection, formulation, paediatric patient or RRT prescription. PD rows are systemic therapy, not intraperitoneal peritonitis therapy.
drugs.jurisdiction: Nebraska institutional adult protocol unless a table explicitly identifies a current product label.

drugStewardship.text: Review kidney function, indication, interactions and OTC products; monitor relevant electrolytes and drug levels. When creatinine estimates are unreliable or precision is critical, consider creatinine–cystatin C estimates or measured GFR. Adjust decisions when kidney function or distribution volume is changing.
